articles.title: Checking a Weidian find before placing a CSSBuy order
articles.description: Follow a spreadsheet find to the seller, match its options and write an order note that leaves little room for substitution.

sections.heading: Start with the exact purchase you mean to make
paragraphs: A link can still work after the seller changes what it offers. Suppose a spreadsheet shows a canvas tote with a shoulder strap. On the live listing there are two options with almost identical thumbnails, but one is the bag alone. Save the seller's option text next to the photo of the set you want. If the strap matters, its inclusion should be explicit before you spend money. A product title seldom describes every option on a multi-variant listing.

sections.heading: Match the source to the order preview
paragraphs: Open the original Weidian listing and keep it available when you paste the link into CSSBuy. Compare the seller, item ID where displayed, option name, quantity and price for the selected configuration. If the preview shows another item, stop at this point. Searching again by title can bring back a similar design from a different seller. A shop page or a collection link also needs an individual product selection before an agent can act on it.

sections.heading: Give the buyer an answerable instruction
paragraphs: CSSBuy's Buy For Me guide describes both link submission and its Expert Buy option for items that search does not retrieve. When manual input is necessary, supply the original link and exact specification. A note such as “Select black canvas with the adjustable strap. If that set has sold out, contact me before purchase” gives the buyer a decision they can carry out. A note like “get the best one” leaves the important choice unresolved.

sections.heading: Keep the final selection with your receipt
paragraphs: Record the option accepted at checkout and the date alongside the original spreadsheet row. If two colours go into the cart, keep each as a separate entry. Later, when the warehouse sends photos, you will be able to point to the correct colour and quantity even if the product page has since changed. Save any answer about included accessories with that order too.

sections.heading: Read the link the way a purchasing agent will
paragraphs: When you open a find from a spreadsheet, several pages may sit between the thumbnail and the seller. A category page can show many related products, a listing can contain a family of variations, and the purchase form can remember a default colour or size. Work through those layers slowly enough to identify the individual offer. In a conventional Weidian URL, the itemID value identifies the listing. It is useful for finding the same listing again, but a listing ID alone rarely records which option you selected.

For example, you might save a row labelled “black desk organizer,” while the seller offers a tray, a pen cup and a bundle. The black finish might apply to all three. If the purchase form defaults to the single pen cup, you could receive exactly what was submitted and still feel the order was wrong. Record the seller's bundle name as well as the colour. If the options have pictures, keep a screenshot of the selected state rather than the unselected hero image.

sections.heading: Compare two finds that look identical
paragraphs: Sellers can use similar photographs for different offers. Suppose two rows in your shortlist show the same green notebook cover. One is a cover only and the other includes the notebook shown inside. Identify whether the underlying item IDs match. If they differ, compare their specifications separately even if the photos look identical. The lower price may reflect a different bundle, material, quantity or size. A different ID does not automatically make an offer worse; it tells you that the selection needs its own verification.

If two rows lead to the same listing, check whether each describes a different variant. You can keep both by recording the item ID and selected option rather than using the URL as the only field. This also helps after delivery. When you receive one notebook and one cover, you can match warehouse photos to the two order lines instead of trying to remember which row was meant to include what.

sections.heading: Resolve a translation ambiguity with a concrete attribute
paragraphs: Machine-translated option labels sometimes preserve colour names while dropping the term that distinguishes a set from an individual piece. Compare the displayed option text with the seller's photographs, but avoid guessing from colour alone. If a single Chinese option label is important, retain the original wording in the purchasing note alongside your short explanation. This gives the agent or merchant the exact words to locate.

Ask a question with an observable answer. “Does this option contain the tray and the separate cup shown in the second image?” can be answered by checking the seller's configuration. “Is this one better?” requires the seller to infer which features you value. When a measurement determines the choice, include the unit and where it is measured. If the seller's answer resolves the issue, attach it to the order record before paying rather than relying on a later translation of the changing product page.

sections.heading: Check quantity and price at the selected state
paragraphs: A spreadsheet often has room for one price, even when the listing offers several configurations. After selecting the intended option, compare the amount shown in CSSBuy against the live seller configuration. Also check the quantity increment. A listing selling pairs is not priced the same way as a listing selling individual components. If you need two pairs, the correct order quantity might be two rather than four. The exact unit is part of the purchase specification.

CSSBuy's Buy For Me flow describes paying for the item and domestic delivery at the purchase stage. Leave international freight separate when comparing seller offers. Imagine that option A costs 55 yuan with 8 yuan domestic shipping and option B costs 60 yuan with local shipping included. The comparable purchase-stage amounts in this example are 63 and 60 yuan. The smaller headline product price is not the smaller first-stage basket. Neither figure tells you what a fully packed international parcel will cost.

sections.heading: Decide when a broken link is worth pursuing
paragraphs: If the CSSBuy form fails to retrieve a listing, first check that you copied the individual seller page rather than a search result, album index or the spreadsheet's own address. Reopen the URL independently and check whether the selected product is still visible. A working merchant page paired with an incomplete import is a different problem from an offer that has been withdrawn. CSSBuy's guide points to Expert Buy when its normal search cannot find an item.

If the original offer is gone, do not silently replace it with a visually similar one. Open the replacement as a new find, identify the seller, compare options and check the size or bundle from scratch. Save the original row as unavailable if you need an audit trail. A buyer who knowingly selects an alternative can evaluate the change. A buyer who assumes the replacement is the original may be unable to explain a discrepancy later.

sections.heading: Use the saved record at warehouse arrival
paragraphs: Once the warehouse images arrive, return to the record made before you paid. First check count and variation, then look at the distinct feature you wanted verified. For the hypothetical tote with a shoulder strap, a photograph of the bag's front alone cannot confirm whether the strap arrived inside. Ask the specific follow-up and provide the order line that includes the accessory. Keep the item out of your international parcel until a concern material to your purchase has been answered.

For future finds, the useful row is short: source listing, seller option, expected contents, selected quantity, price date, special instruction and order number. A spreadsheet with these fields can remain useful even after the seller changes an image or price. It records the decision you made and the evidence necessary to check it, without turning a discovery list into a claim that the goods have already been inspected.

articles.title: Buying from 1688 through CSSBuy when the supplier sets a minimum
articles.description: Work out which unit the seller is quoting, what quantity qualifies and whether a multi-unit purchase makes sense for your parcel.

sections.heading: Read the quantity beside the price
paragraphs: A price that looks right for one household item can belong to a larger quantity tier. CSSBuy specifically tells buyers that many 1688 suppliers impose minimums. Check the live offer for the selected variation and quantity before multiplying a number copied from a spreadsheet. If the listing describes a pack, establish how many pieces the pack contains. Two packs of three and two individual pieces create very different purchase orders.

sections.heading: Check how colours count
paragraphs: Imagine a supplier displaying three colours and a two-unit minimum. You want one blue and one green. The headline minimum alone cannot tell you whether the supplier permits mixed colours to qualify. Ask CSSBuy to confirm the combination with the seller if the live order form is unclear. Where matching colours matter, add an instruction that substitutions require approval. Keep the answer with the two line items so you can inspect the correct split at arrival.

sections.heading: Compare the complete basket
paragraphs: For illustration, a hypothetical single-unit offer costs 45 yuan plus 8 yuan for domestic delivery. A wholesale alternative at 30 yuan each with a two-unit minimum and 10 yuan delivery costs 70 yuan for the basket. The wholesale unit price is lower, but the basket costs 17 yuan more before international shipping. Consider how much use you have for the second item and whether it adds another bulky box. These numbers illustrate the calculation and are independent of any live CSSBuy rate.

sections.heading: Agree on what can be inspected
paragraphs: CSSBuy flags a different quality-control standard for purchases from 1688. If you need an individual count, a label photo or confirmation of a specific accessory, ask what can be checked for this order before purchasing in bulk. For a carton of identical goods, a photograph of the sealed outer carton alone cannot establish the contents of each package. Keep any inspection limits in mind when deciding how many units to buy.

sections.heading: Model the purchase as a basket, then compare the unit
paragraphs: For a useful comparison, give each seller its own row and write down the exact version you are pricing. Multiply the amount per selling unit by the number of selling units. Include domestic shipping at the displayed quantity and record the number of usable pieces that will arrive. If the merchant sells a pack, converting the final basket into a cost per usable piece lets you compare it with a merchant selling single pieces. Keep international freight as a separate estimate until the warehouse has measurements.

Consider a hypothetical pack of six plain storage pouches. One supplier charges 72 yuan for a pack and 8 yuan for local delivery. The basket totals 80 yuan, which is about 13.33 yuan per pouch. Another supplier offers individual pouches at 14 yuan with 4 yuan local delivery per order. If you need six, its comparable basket is 88 yuan. If you need two, the single-piece offer totals 32 yuan and the first merchant still requires 80. The demand you actually have changes the decision. No live supplier price or CSSBuy fee is implied by those sample figures.

sections.heading: Read a tier boundary without inventing a discount
paragraphs: A tiered display might state one amount for a small order and a different one above a threshold. Select the intended quantity on the live page and inspect the resulting amount. If the display changes only after choosing a colour or specification, capture that state. Do not multiply the largest advertised discount by a quantity that cannot earn it. Where the imported agent page and live seller option disagree, pause and request the amount the seller will accept for the configured order.

For example, imagine a seller showing 20 yuan for quantities two through nine and 16 yuan from ten units onward. Nine units at the first tier total 180 yuan, while ten at the second total 160 yuan before delivery. That surprising result deserves confirmation from the actual checkout or seller. Even if confirmed, the extra unit still needs packing, storage and a use. A threshold calculation can reveal a question; it cannot verify a merchant's current terms.

sections.heading: Check the geometry of a multi-unit purchase
paragraphs: Freight matters most for pieces that use more space than their weight suggests. Six fabric pouches might nest almost flat, while six rigid gift boxes may require a much larger carton. Ask for the likely packed format if it affects your budget. Can a decorative sleeve be packed flat? Must a protective insert stay in place? Will the seller dispatch a carton of individually boxed pieces? Write these as questions about the specific goods rather than assuming the warehouse can reconstruct the seller's packaging later.

If the individual units need to be presentable, do not treat all retail materials as disposable in your estimate. Compare the complete carton with the amount you would genuinely pay for the same number of usable items locally. Keep the comparison in one currency and record the exchange rate you used for your own budget. Check the agent checkout separately for its current conversion and charges.

sections.heading: Plan inspection around the kind of error that matters
paragraphs: A carton can be correct in total quantity and wrong in assortment. If you ordered three black pouches and three white pouches, six pieces in a photograph settle only the first question. Give the agent the exact split in your purchasing notes and ask what inspection evidence can reasonably be supplied under the applicable 1688 standard. If each pouch is sealed and the outer package lacks a colour code, finding the answer may require handling that affects presentation. Decide in advance whether that is acceptable.

For custom sizes, direct attention to the actual point of variation. A set may come with short and long straps under the same product name. A detail photo of a logo offers little evidence about strap length. Request a clear label or measurement if feasible. If the supplier cannot confirm the configuration or the available inspection cannot address your concern, reducing the order size or choosing a different listing may be more practical than accepting a large uncertain basket.

sections.heading: Decide whether a sample answers the real question
paragraphs: Buyers sometimes look for a single sample before committing to a larger quantity. Confirm whether that specific supplier sells one, what variant it represents and whether a later production run would have the same specification. One sample may help you evaluate dimensions, colour under your lighting or how a fastening feels. It is weak evidence for the consistency of twenty unseen pieces. Keep those two questions distinct when setting a budget for a trial.

If a separate sample listing is offered, record the connection to the bulk listing and compare the option text. A photograph shared between two product pages does not establish that both will supply the same material or pack size. Keep the seller's confirmation with the order record. Then, if the trial meets your needs, recheck the bulk minimum, price and lead time at the point you are ready to reorder.

sections.heading: Keep the final purchasing instruction short enough to use
paragraphs: A useful line can read, “Please confirm whether one pack of six can contain three black and three white units. If mixed colours are unavailable, contact me before purchasing.” Follow it with the exact source option labels and the quantity as the order form wants it. Leave the detailed arithmetic in your own notes. The person placing the purchase needs the intended configuration and the boundary on acceptable changes.

Before approving, you should be able to name the expected number of usable pieces, the maximum basket you agreed to and how any required mix will be checked. When the goods reach the warehouse, compare the received configuration with that record. Those three details protect against the most expensive errors in a wholesale-style order: buying more than you need, buying the wrong version in quantity, or discovering too late that the assortment cannot be checked.

articles.title: What to put in a CSSBuy Expert Buy request
articles.description: Prepare a manual purchase request when the normal product search cannot retrieve the seller's listing.

sections.heading: Identify the exact offer
paragraphs: CSSBuy directs customers to Expert Buy when ordinary item search fails. Begin with the direct seller URL, the seller's displayed product name and a screenshot of the exact option if available. If you found the item in an album, identify the individual item and selected specification. A link to a seller's entire collection asks the person placing the order to make a decision you could have settled yourself.

sections.heading: Translate the buying decision into fields
paragraphs: Write each variable separately. For a hypothetical fabric order this might be the seller's colour number, sold length per unit, number of units and whether a continuous piece is essential. Including both the seller's wording and a plain-language description makes an ambiguous translation easier to resolve. Avoid treating a picture of several pieces as evidence of the quantity sold. If a price depends on dimensions, ask for confirmation of the configured price.

sections.heading: Decide which changes need your approval
paragraphs: A useful note names the action if the selected version is unavailable. For example, ask CSSBuy to contact you before accepting a different finish or a higher price. If either finish is acceptable but only within a budget, give that specific instruction. CSSBuy describes an order-note channel and says it may request more information. Monitor the message associated with the order while it is being purchased.

sections.heading: Check the order summary once it exists
paragraphs: Compare the confirmation with the request before assuming the seller has accepted every detail. Find the order number, recorded quantity and selected option. Keep any agreement about a custom specification in the same place. If the eventual warehouse photo raises a question, the original request tells you what CSSBuy was asked to buy and the seller's answer tells you what was actually promised.

sections.heading: Decide whether manual purchasing solves your particular problem
paragraphs: Expert Buy is useful when the ordinary importer cannot create the right purchase from a seller link. First establish whether the difficulty is finding the page, reading the options, or obtaining information the merchant has never supplied. If you have no link and only a picture, a manual purchase form cannot magically identify its original seller. If you have a clear source but the agent's search cannot retrieve it, a direct link, specification and price give the buyer a concrete starting point. If the merchant has not explained what a bundle includes, an enquiry to the merchant must still resolve that gap.

Try opening the source yourself and select the complete configuration. Does the seller show a price, a way to choose the specification, and a quantity unit? Write down the answer for each. A shopping agent can ask follow-up questions, but a request with these foundations gives both sides a better chance of spotting a mismatch before payment. Be especially careful with social posts or album images that present several products in one picture.

sections.heading: Describe a real option in a short block of text
paragraphs: Imagine ordering three metres of cotton canvas from a seller whose photos show ten colours on a swatch card. The buy request should identify the card and the number of the chosen colour, the width of the fabric, the selling unit, the quantity you intend and whether you need one continuous length. If the seller sells half-metre units, six units may be required to create that length. Buying three units because you need three metres could yield half as much fabric as planned.

A workable note is: “Swatch 07, natural canvas, listed width 140 cm. I need one continuous cut three metres long. Please confirm the number of seller units and contact me if it will come in separate pieces.” This is a hypothetical example, not a CSSBuy form requirement. It captures the choice the agent needs to communicate and the condition that would change your decision. It avoids unnecessary background about what you plan to make with the fabric.

sections.heading: Distinguish a quoted price from an approved ceiling
paragraphs: A price shown in an album might apply to the base model, a single accessory or an older promotion. Record where you saw it and what it appeared to include. If you are willing to accept a limited increase, explicitly state that the agent should confirm the final total before purchasing when the new price is above your budget. If you expect domestic delivery to be separate, account for it separately. This prevents a later disagreement arising simply because one amount included local postage and another did not.

Avoid giving an open-ended instruction to pay whatever is necessary. On a manual order, even a small variation can change the seller's quote substantially. A custom length, an extra attachment or a change in pack size might be priced differently. Decide ahead of time whether a price change cancels the request, requires your approval or is acceptable within a stated limit. Keep that decision attached to the seller's response.

sections.heading: Handle alternate spellings, numbers and images
paragraphs: An option can be uniquely identified by a picture and still be easy to misread in text. Codes such as O1 and 01, similar translations of cream and beige, or labels using measurements without units create avoidable uncertainty. Copy the seller's exact option text, add the unit you intend and include the relevant image if the order channel accepts it. If you supply several pictures, state which image identifies the selection and which simply shows the feature you want confirmed.

If an image includes a second item as decoration, say explicitly whether you are ordering that accessory. For example, “the wooden base only, without the lamp pictured above it” is more useful than “same as photo.” If you need a compatible set, identify both seller options and ask whether they are sold together, purchased separately or supplied in a fixed combination. Do not rely on the purchasing agent to infer a bundle from styling photography.

sections.heading: Interpret a request for further information
paragraphs: When CSSBuy sends a clarification, read the question in terms of the decision the buyer cannot make. If the merchant's selected colour is unavailable, replying “yes” might mean either that you understand or that you authorize a substitution. Instead, answer with the action: “Wait for the original colour and tell me the expected restock date,” or “Cancel this line if the selected version cannot be purchased.” If multiple order lines exist, include the item reference.

If the merchant proposes a substitute, compare the attributes that mattered in the first place. A replacement of the same colour could be a different material or unit count. Ask the merchant, through the agent where appropriate, for the changed attributes and revised total. Keep the original and proposed choices separately in your own record so that, if you do approve the substitution, the warehouse will later have the correct comparison.

sections.heading: Convert the purchase note into a warehouse check
paragraphs: After a manual order is accepted, take the few attributes central to your decision and turn them into inspection questions. For the fabric example, the selected colour code, number of pieces and continuous length matter more than whether the folded package looks tidy. Some of those questions may be answerable visually while others need a measurement or opening. Ask what verification is actually available and what it would cost before expecting it as part of ordinary handling.

If the seller supplied a written confirmation, retain it with the order number. When the goods arrive, compare the confirmation, purchase record and actual pictures. A discrepancy among those three has a clear starting point for support. A neatly written request earns its keep twice: first when the buyer has to place the order, and later when you have to decide whether the specific item in the warehouse is the one you authorized.

articles.title: Reading CSSBuy warehouse QC photos for size and missing parts
articles.description: Use the order specification and a clearly described measurement to resolve a warehouse-photo question before shipment.

sections.heading: Decide what a photograph can settle
paragraphs: For a jacket, it may be possible to read the size label, count the buttons and compare the colour panels. A photograph alone is a poor way to determine how the shoulders will fit. List the questions you need answered and choose an observable test for each. CSSBuy describes inspection and photography after warehouse arrival. Check which views were supplied for your order and ask about the availability and price of additional work when needed.

sections.heading: Match the photo to the purchased variation
paragraphs: Start with the order number and source option. A main listing photo may show a jacket with detachable trim even when the lower-priced option excludes it. Look for the trim only if the purchased specification includes it. If several similar jackets arrived, pair each image set with its own order number. Label a concern precisely enough that another person can find it without reviewing your whole cart.

sections.heading: Name both endpoints of a measurement
paragraphs: If sleeve length matters, explain whether you mean shoulder seam to cuff or neckline to cuff. For a raglan sleeve these are different measurements. Request a clear view of both tape endpoints and the unit. Compare a garment laid flat with another garment measured the same way. A body circumference, a half-width on a table and the seller's recommended body size are three different figures.

sections.heading: Use the result while the item is in the warehouse
paragraphs: If a discrepancy appears, keep the image, the selected option and a short explanation together. Contact CSSBuy on the relevant order before submitting that item for international delivery. Its public FAQ describes a short warehouse return window and conditions for return to the seller. A pending photo question is worth addressing immediately, even if you plan to hold other approved items for consolidation.

sections.heading: Work from a garment you already wear
paragraphs: If fit is the reason for asking for a measurement, choose a piece you own that fits the way you want this purchase to fit. A loose overshirt and a fitted dress shirt can have the same nominal size while needing very different measurements. Lay your reference garment flat, close any fastening that affects its shape, and note how you positioned it. A buyer measuring a favourite jacket while wearing it will not have a comparable reference for a warehouse garment laid flat on a table.

Select the few dimensions that drive the decision. For a jacket that pulls across the chest, flat chest width may matter more than total length. For trousers that fit everywhere but at the ankle, inner leg length and leg opening may tell you more than the generic size label. Save your own reference values and units. The customer service agent does not need your personal body measurements to photograph a seam-to-seam garment measurement.

sections.heading: Specify the path of the tape
paragraphs: Write one instruction for each dimension that cannot be read from the supplied views. A flat half-chest measurement might run horizontally from one underarm point to the other with the jacket closed and lying naturally. Back length could be taken from the base of the rear collar to the bottom hem along the middle. If you measure from the top of the collar at home but ask the warehouse to measure from its base, the difference will include the collar itself.

A tape photographed at an angle can make a result difficult to read. Ask for the zero point and endpoint to appear in the same plane as the garment, with the relevant markings legible. An elastic waistband deserves an extra specification: do you need the relaxed flat width or a moderately stretched measurement? Stretching force is hard to standardize remotely. Compare the relaxed measurement first and ask the seller about the garment's intended fit if uncertainty remains.

sections.heading: Use the right arithmetic and keep the unit
paragraphs: Suppose your own buttoned jacket measures 55 centimetres across the chest when flat, while the warehouse photo appears to show 53 centimetres using the same endpoints. The observable difference is 2 centimetres in flat width. Simply doubling each flat figure suggests about 4 centimetres of difference around the garment, but cut, seams and thickness affect how much ease you actually feel. Avoid treating that calculation as a prediction of exactly how a tailored or lined piece will wear.

Now suppose the seller's chart lists 110 centimetres as a chest measurement. If that field means the garment's full circumference, it may correspond roughly to a flat 55-centimetre comparison. If it means recommended body chest size, a direct comparison is inappropriate. Identify what the chart measures before asking for a return on the basis of two numbers that describe different things. Keep centimetres and inches labelled consistently, especially if the tape displays both.

sections.heading: Inspect a set as a set
paragraphs: A product photo may show a jacket, belt and removable hood. Check which of them were actually included in your chosen option. If the seller's order says three separate components, look for three visible components or a credible explanation that one is inside a pocket or packet. Ask for the smallest additional view needed to resolve the uncertainty. Opening every sealed accessory could alter the packaging more than your question requires.

Use the order number when several items share accessories. Two apparently identical straps might belong to different bag sizes. Compare width, colour, hardware or the option code if those details distinguish them. A flat lay showing one bag and a strap confirms physical presence together in the photograph; it does not prove compatibility between two different models. If the connection is important, ask whether the fastening can be checked within the service being offered.

sections.heading: Decide which discrepancies are material
paragraphs: A measurement difference matters in context. A small variation at the bottom of a loose garment may not change how you wear it. The same difference in a closely fitted sleeve opening might prevent it fitting over a watch or another layer. Set a realistic personal lower or upper limit before seeing the warehouse result. That protects you from trying to rationalize an unsuitable piece simply because you have already waited for it to arrive.

If the measurements are borderline, distinguish uncertainty from a demonstrated error. A hidden zero point, a folded hem or a tape laid along the wrong seam leaves the first result inconclusive. Ask for one corrected measurement using clear endpoints. If reliable evidence shows the item misses a specification you agreed with the seller, send the seller's stated dimension, your selected size and the relevant warehouse image through the order's support channel. The response will depend on the merchant and applicable return conditions.

sections.heading: Preserve only the evidence needed for a decision
paragraphs: Name saved images by order and feature rather than by generic camera filenames. A label photo, a full front view and a measurement view have different purposes. Keep the original files when possible so that tiny tape markings remain legible. If you annotate one, retain a clean copy and state whether your note is an observation, a comparison with your own garment or a question for the seller.

When you decide to ship, record why the evidence was adequate. “Flat chest 54 cm against a 53 cm minimum; belt and hood visible” captures a verifiable decision. If you request a return, keep the order on hold from international submission until the return request is understood. Check your other warehouse items independently. An unresolved sleeve measurement should not be allowed to obscure the storage deadline or shipment decision for the rest of your parcel.

sections.heading: Keep a reusable measurement profile
paragraphs: If your first order gives you a good fit, measure the delivered garment yourself and compare it with the warehouse image. Record any difference that arose from your measuring technique. A repeatable set of reference measurements for each type of garment makes the next warehouse enquiry shorter and helps you interpret a photograph without assuming that every seller uses the same sizing chart.

sources.title: CSSBuy · Official storage and returns FAQ

articles.title: Managing CSSBuy storage when items arrive on different days
articles.description: Calculate each item's warehouse deadline and compare storage extension with a partial shipment.

sections.heading: Put a date against each order
paragraphs: CSSBuy's FAQ starts the standard free storage period at the In Warehouse status. A purchase date, payment receipt or domestic carrier scan can all be earlier. Record the warehouse date shown for each order and check the account's actual deadline. An order you placed later may arrive first. Sorting a list by purchase date therefore gives a misleading picture of which item needs attention.

sections.heading: Count extensions by the unit CSSBuy bills
paragraphs: The public FAQ lists 90 free days and a subsequent charge of 15 yuan per order per month. Check the current amount and availability for the specific order before paying. By simple arithmetic, four independently billable orders at that published rate would total 60 yuan for one month. Four pieces recorded under one order should prompt a check of the account's billing unit before you apply the same calculation.

sections.heading: Compare three practical choices
paragraphs: Consider a box containing items A and B, with item C delayed at the seller. You can send A and B together now, wait within their free periods, or look at extending the older order. Obtain comparable shipping estimates for the partial and complete boxes. Also consider whether C actually has a reliable arrival date. Spending on an extension based on an unconfirmed restock can leave you facing the same decision again.

sections.heading: Confirm that the deadline actually moved
paragraphs: CSSBuy warns that items past the free period without shipment or extension can be treated as abandoned and destroyed. Record the extension receipt and the new date shown against the affected order. If the account still shows the old deadline, contact support promptly with the order number and payment detail. A note in your own spreadsheet cannot substitute for the warehouse accepting the extension.

sections.heading: Build a storage register that prevents a forgotten order
paragraphs: Give each CSSBuy order one row, even when several orders came from the same seller or have identical product names. Record the order number, the date it reached In Warehouse, the date shown for expiry, the declared quantity and its current decision. A useful decision might be “accepted for next parcel,” “waiting for a replacement” or “need a size measurement.” This last field explains why the item is still there and who needs to act. A generic note saying “hold” becomes hard to interpret a month later.

Keep the warehouse deadline and a personal decision date in different columns. You may want to decide ahead of a holiday, trip or weekend when you cannot check your account, even if the warehouse deadline is later. Sorting by your decision date helps you act before the last opportunity. Update the entry after each status change rather than resetting the whole sheet whenever a new item arrives.

sections.heading: Calculate the cost of waiting for the right group
paragraphs: Suppose three individually billed orders are near the end of the free period and you are waiting on one more seller. At the rate published in the FAQ, one extra month for all three would be 45 yuan. Two months at that same rate would be 90 yuan. Confirm the applicable price and any renewal conditions before making that commitment. These examples use the published unit of billing and do not imply that every item in a mixed account is eligible on identical terms.

Now obtain a current estimate for shipping those three orders together and another for the planned complete group. You may not yet know the final dimensions of the fourth item. Test two plausible sizes rather than giving an unknown box a weight of zero. Compare the complete choices, including any extension, packing or second shipment. If the freight saving depends on the fourth item arriving before the next month, find out what evidence supports that assumption.

sections.heading: Decide which item actually needs the extension
paragraphs: An account can contain a bulky low-value item, a valuable compact item and a small accessory with a long remaining free period. Extending every line because one is near expiry can waste money. Work down the register in deadline order. Ask whether the older item can go now, whether it should wait with a justified extension, or whether an existing unresolved problem needs support before either choice is reasonable. Then consider the younger items separately.

If you decide to ship two items and extend one, note the order numbers explicitly. After completing the actions, reopen the warehouse list. Check which entries moved to the parcel and which remains stored. If two visually identical products came from different orders, rely on their references to verify that the oldest was actually sent. A selected thumbnail may be a poor guide when the account contains repeated purchases.

sections.heading: Handle an item with an unresolved seller issue
paragraphs: Storage time and the merchant's return conditions are separate concerns. Waiting within a generous storage period can still allow a tighter seller window to close. When a photo reveals a possible wrong variation, contact the relevant order as soon as you see it and ask whether a return or exchange is available. Keep the storage deadline visible during the investigation. A support conversation about the product should not be assumed to pause warehouse billing or extend an expiry date.

For an exchange, ask how the returned original and the incoming replacement will appear in the account. You need to know which record still holds a physical item and which date applies to the updated entry. Do not simply overwrite the older order with the replacement's expected arrival. Save the confirmed return and check the replacement when it is actually stored. This is especially important if your decision to delay other goods depends on the replacement joining their parcel.

sections.heading: Choose a reminder that leads to an action
paragraphs: A calendar reminder should tell you what to do when it appears. “Review order A, get current freight for A plus B, and decide whether to pay for a one-month extension” is more effective than “CSSBuy deadline.” Include the relevant order number and the deadline as displayed on the account. Keep personal data and payment details out of a calendar entry shared with other people.

If you miss an earlier reminder, review the live inventory promptly rather than assuming your estimate still applies. Check whether the order remains available to ship or extend. If the interface is unclear, contact CSSBuy with the order reference and the precise deadline you can see. The official FAQ explains the consequence of items being treated as abandoned; it does not warrant that an expired item can be recovered after disposal.

sections.heading: Verify a partial shipment before closing your record
paragraphs: After submitting some goods for overseas delivery, keep the parcel reference next to the relevant order numbers and confirm that the outstanding warehouse entries correspond to the items you intentionally left behind. If the parcel still requires payment or a packing decision, maintain that as its own follow-up. Completing the first step in the interface may leave an action before the package can actually move.

Once the remaining order is extended, record its revised expiry and keep evidence of payment. Compare that evidence with the live account if anything appears inconsistent. The practical aim is to know, at any point, which physical goods remain at the warehouse, who is waiting for what, when the next deadline arrives and how much it will cost to wait. With those details visible, decisions about combining orders become budget choices rather than last-minute attempts to save forgotten inventory.

sections.heading: Leave a deadline record after consolidation
paragraphs: For any group approaching expiry, take a dated copy of the relevant inventory entries before submitting them. If a payment or parcel review fails, compare the current inventory with that list and check whether the orders still require storage action. This helps distinguish an item genuinely released for shipment from one accidentally left behind when a parcel selection did not finish.

sources.title: CSSBuy · Official storage and returns FAQ

articles.title: Requesting a CSSBuy seller return before the warehouse window closes
articles.description: Identify the seller's conditions, document the issue and check the domestic return costs before authorizing a return.

sections.heading: Start with the warehouse arrival
paragraphs: CSSBuy's public FAQ describes three conditions for its usual warehouse return assistance. The seller must accept a return, the item must have been in the warehouse for less than seven days, and return shipping must be covered. Check the receipt date and seller conditions as soon as a concern appears. Do not use your planned international ship date as the start of the clock.

sections.heading: Describe exactly why the item is going back
paragraphs: If you ordered a two-piece set and see one piece, ask first whether the second is inside the package or arriving separately. If you ordered a blue item and the label identifies a different seller colour, supply both option names and the corresponding photo. A change of mind and a discrepancy with the order are distinct explanations. Report the facts you can support and ask how the seller will handle that reason.

sections.heading: Compare a refund with an exchange
paragraphs: For a low-cost item, the domestic postage may be material to the amount recovered. Ask for the return cost, any deduction, and whether a replacement requires a second delivery charge. If you want an exchange, confirm that the desired variant is available before agreeing to send the original back. Waiting for a replacement may also change the storage plans for unrelated goods.

sections.heading: Keep the evidence until the transaction is reconciled
paragraphs: Save the order number, seller's response, approved action, domestic tracking if available, and eventual credit or replacement record. If the goods have already been exported, use CSSBuy's after-sales guidance for that stage. It mentions purchase receipts and warranty documents for relevant defects arising after use. A warehouse return request and an overseas warranty enquiry need different evidence and may carry different costs.

sections.heading: Identify the precise object of the return
paragraphs: Write down the seller order, the CSSBuy order and the item you want returned. For a single-item purchase those may seem interchangeable. For a set of three or a purchase containing several colours, the difference matters. A merchant might require an entire set back, even when one component is wrong; or it might agree to replace only the missing part. Ask which physical goods must be sent and whether the original accessories and packaging must accompany them.

Take a practical example: an organizer sold with six removable dividers arrives with five visible in the warehouse photo. It may be possible that the last divider is nested inside the base. Ask for a count before describing the set as defective. If the sixth piece is genuinely missing, the merchant might offer to send that component domestically. Compare the delay and cost of that solution with returning the whole product. The appropriate remedy depends on what was promised and what actually arrived.

sections.heading: Collect evidence for the reason you are giving
paragraphs: A variant dispute starts with the seller's selected option and the agent order confirmation. A quantity dispute starts with the sales unit and the number of pieces received. A visible condition problem calls for a clear image of the affected area and, when useful, the outer packaging. Save these records separately. A photograph showing a dent does not prove that a different size was ordered, and a seller option screenshot cannot show damage to the delivered piece.

Describe the mismatch using ordinary observable facts. “The order is for the 30 cm model, the outer label reads 25 cm and the warehouse tape also shows approximately 25 cm” gives the agent something concrete to present to the merchant. If the tape endpoint is hidden, explain that the result is unclear and ask for a corrected view. A smaller amount of reliable evidence is usually more persuasive than a long sequence of pictures with no indication of what each proves.

sections.heading: Compare refund, replacement and acceptance with numbers
paragraphs: Suppose a hypothetical item cost 65 yuan and return postage would cost you 12 yuan. If the seller agrees to refund the full item price, the merchandise refund less that postage would be 53 yuan before any other applicable charges. If domestic delivery on the original purchase was separate, check whether it is refundable too; do not silently include it in the 65. A promise that “the item is refundable” does not on its own settle every associated charge.

For an exchange, check whether you would owe return shipping, a new delivery cost, or a price difference for the replacement size. Also ask whether the correct model is in stock and when the replacement could be sent. Accepting a small seller concession may be sensible only if the item remains useful for the purpose you bought it for. A partial refund on a case that does not fit your device may offer little practical value.

sections.heading: Ask the merchant one question at a time
paragraphs: An initial message can include the order number, receipt date, reason for return and your preferred solution. Ask the agent to confirm eligibility while the item remains at the warehouse. Once the merchant answers, follow up on any costs or requirements that remain unclear. Trying to negotiate a refund percentage, exchange size, postage and future discount all at once makes a short response such as “yes” difficult to interpret.

If the seller authorizes return, ask what address and process the agent will use, and whether the warehouse can retain evidence of dispatch. Do not send goods independently or share unrelated customer information. The item is under warehouse control, and the agent needs to associate its physical return with the correct seller case. If the part is included in a larger shipment plan, remove it from the planned international selection until the case is settled.

sections.heading: Understand what each status demonstrates
paragraphs: A request being submitted means the seller has been asked for a remedy. Authorization means the seller agreed under specified conditions. Domestic return tracking means merchandise has been sent back. A refund entry means money was credited through a particular channel. An exchange requires the additional step of verifying the replacement. Treat them as separate checkpoints so that one update does not get mistaken for completion of the whole case.

For a replacement, inspect the new unit against the agreed specification just as you would inspect the original. A second warehouse arrival might have a new reference. Keep the original seller agreement linked to that reference, especially if the merchant promised a different size or a specific accessory. If the replacement still has an issue, the value of that paper trail is that the agent can see what the merchant agreed to correct.

sections.heading: Keep unrelated items moving when appropriate
paragraphs: A single return can delay a combined parcel unnecessarily. Recheck your other items' storage periods and calculate whether waiting for the replacement still makes sense. A heavy box with several ready items and one uncertain low-cost accessory presents a different decision from a parcel meant specifically to contain a matching set. Price the partial shipment and later combination before assuming all goods must wait together.

If the seller declines a return, ask for the stated reason and review the applicable seller conditions. If the issue is no longer an ordinary domestic return because the goods have gone abroad, consult CSSBuy's after-sales policy for the relevant stage and retain receipts and warranty materials where applicable. Close the warehouse case only when the final action and its financial result are clear. Your record should show exactly what the merchant accepted, what was sent, what was credited and whether a replacement still needs attention.

sections.heading: Reconcile the final domestic postage
paragraphs: If the merchant authorizes a return, compare the agreed return-postage amount with the final debit. If they differ, ask whether the actual carrier fee changed or whether the debit covers an additional service. Retain the seller's acceptance alongside the refund record. This is particularly helpful on sets where only one component was returned and the original order remains partly active.
