articles.title: Using CSSBuy Ship For Me for goods you purchased yourself
articles.description: Match a seller shipment to your forwarding order and check package choices before the international leg.

sections.heading: Identify who is placing the purchase
paragraphs: Ship For Me serves buyers ordering from the seller themselves and forwarding purchases to the CSSBuy warehouse. If you need CSSBuy to buy from the seller, its Buy For Me instructions describe that separate process. Make this decision before paying a merchant. An order you already placed generally needs delivery and identification details for forwarding, not a second purchase request for the same goods.

sections.heading: Copy the account's current address
paragraphs: CSSBuy directs customers to their member area for the warehouse address. Use the address supplied to your account and copy all required receiving details, including any identifier displayed. Keep the Chinese characters intact where the merchant expects them. A warehouse address copied from an old tutorial could omit the field that ties the seller's package to you. Confirm the saved merchant address before dispatch.

sections.heading: Track the incoming boxes independently
paragraphs: If a merchant splits an order, record every domestic tracking number alongside its item list. One delivered box does not prove that every item in the merchant order has arrived. Retain the seller receipt and the carrier's delivery information. If the warehouse cannot identify a box, these details give support something specific to match against its receiving records.

sections.heading: Give the warehouse packaging instructions that fit the goods
paragraphs: CSSBuy describes consolidation, vacuum packaging and reinforcement on its forwarding page. Decide separately for each item whether its retail packaging has value, whether compression could damage its shape and which fragile surfaces need protection. For example, preserve a rigid presentation box while asking about compressing a separate group of plain garments. Verify the resulting parcel details and quote before authorizing overseas shipment.

sections.heading: Map the two transactions before entering an address
paragraphs: With an independently purchased item you have a transaction with the seller and a forwarding arrangement with the warehouse. Your merchant account records the product, payment and local delivery. Your warehouse account identifies the incoming goods and the eventual international parcel. Keep the corresponding references side by side. If the seller sends the wrong product, the original sales record matters. If a correctly addressed box reaches the warehouse but cannot be found in your account, the receiving records matter.

This distinction becomes especially important when the forwarding purchase is supposed to join other products the agent bought for you. The final parcel may be a convenient combined shipment, yet the agent was not the original buyer for every item inside. Record which seller communication and payment records you control directly. Then, if a question arises, you can supply the evidence yourself instead of waiting for an agent to look up a merchant payment it never made.

sections.heading: Enter the receiving fields without guessing
paragraphs: Use the warehouse details displayed in your own member center. Preserve the displayed recipient, contact data, regional fields and any required identifying text. A merchant address form may divide province, city, district and detailed street address into separate boxes. Follow the corresponding fields carefully and inspect the merchant's final saved address as a complete string. Copying the correct street but omitting the account reference can create a box that reaches the building without being easy to match to you.

If the merchant rejects a field, ask CSSBuy how to enter the current details in that particular form. Avoid substituting a familiar city, removing characters to make the text look shorter or borrowing a recipient identity from a public screenshot. Check before the seller dispatches, while an error may be easier to correct. For an order already sent, share the actual label details and domestic tracking privately with the agent for advice.

sections.heading: Make a package register when one seller sends multiple boxes
paragraphs: Suppose you buy two shelves and a set of fittings in one merchant order. The seller sends each shelf separately and puts the fittings in the first carton. Create entries for carton one and carton two, each with its own tracking number and contents. If the first carton reaches the warehouse and the second remains in transit, the seller's order may still look partly complete. Keeping carton-level detail prevents a single delivery event from being mistaken for receipt of both shelves.

If the merchant changes a tracking number, retain the old and new numbers and mark which is active. If two cartons cannot be distinguished by their labels, ask the seller for the dispatch details it actually has instead of guessing their contents. That way the warehouse can match physical boxes against reliable carrier information. Once the items appear in your account, compare quantities with the independent order receipt before approving consolidation.

sections.heading: Decide what inspection can reasonably establish
paragraphs: CSSBuy's forwarding page describes a QC service that can photograph goods. Ask what is available for the product and packing you received. For the shelf example, a label photo might confirm the advertised finish, while counting fittings could require opening a sealed packet. Opening the box may affect how safely it can be repacked, or the merchant may have particular return conditions. Resolve these questions before asking the warehouse to unpack more than necessary.

If an actual problem appears, record whether it is damage to the outer shipping carton, a missing accessory, an incorrect model or an issue you cannot verify visually. Contact the merchant from the purchase account if its authorization is needed. Ask CSSBuy what it can do on the forwarding side, such as identifying the parcel or providing available evidence. Do not assume that responsibility for a merchant return automatically transfers when goods enter a forwarding warehouse.

sections.heading: Test consolidation against the contents you have
paragraphs: Once every expected incoming box is recorded, look at the actual product shapes. Two flat shelves may be economical to pack together, while a small fragile object could require protective clearance that changes the outer dimensions. Compare the available combined option with appropriate separate parcels. If the goods include anything subject to transport restrictions, check the eligible lines for the actual contents before approving the plan.

Where packaging choices matter, refer to the individual item numbers. For example, instruct the warehouse to retain corner protection on the two shelves and keep the small fittings in a sealed bag. Ask whether redundant outer shipping materials can be removed without exposing the finished surfaces. A generic instruction to discard all boxes could remove protection that would cost more to replace than the freight saved. Ask for updated packed information where available.

sections.heading: Review both addresses and both legs before payment
paragraphs: Your merchant's domestic shipping address and your international receiving address serve different routes. Check that the overseas parcel uses the correct personal destination, contact information and postal details. A domestic seller tracking number ends at the warehouse; your later parcel should have its own shipping reference. Maintain that distinction in your records when looking up tracking or asking a carrier about delivery.

Before releasing the international package, check its item list against the original merchant receipts, the warehouse entries and any goods the agent purchased separately. Make sure a seller's delayed second carton has not been left behind unintentionally. Save the parcel reference with the list of items you approved. A complete record lets you answer three different questions later: what the merchant agreed to sell, which domestic parcels the warehouse received and what the overseas parcel was supposed to contain. Those answers make forwarding considerably easier to manage if any one handoff needs investigation.

sections.heading: Separate the merchant receipt from the warehouse handoff
paragraphs: If a merchant later asks for proof of a missing domestic shipment, send the carrier details for the incoming package and the seller order reference. If an overseas carrier asks what was in the final carton, use the completed parcel's inventory and waybill instead. A forwarding file works well when it lets you produce either record independently without exposing unrelated purchases or relying on screenshots copied from someone else's account.

articles.title: Choosing CSSBuy vacuum packaging or parcel reinforcement
articles.description: Plan a mixed parcel around shape, protection and billable dimensions using the packing options CSSBuy actually describes.

sections.heading: Think about the space that sets the box size
paragraphs: Vacuum packing may reduce the space occupied by compressible clothing. The benefit depends on what else is in the parcel. If a rigid box determines the outer length and width, flattening an adjacent garment may leave the parcel dimensions unchanged. Compare what you expect to happen to each dimension, and ask the warehouse about the packed result before relying on any estimated saving.

sections.heading: Mark items that need to keep their shape
paragraphs: A structured accessory, a moulded insert and a folded cotton shirt have different needs. Identify which items can be compressed and which should stay in their retail protection. CSSBuy offers reinforcement and describes bubble wrapping for fragile goods. Ask what is feasible for the specific parcel. Extra padding can increase dimensions, but replacing a damaged object may cost more than the freight difference.

sections.heading: Make instructions intelligible on a mixed order
paragraphs: For example, specify “Keep the board game's rigid box and protect its corners. The two cotton shirts may be compressed separately.” Include the item references and avoid vague directions such as “remove all boxes” if an exception matters. Packaging removal can be difficult to reverse. If a retail box must remain suitable for a gift, state whether the box itself needs an outer protective layer.

sections.heading: Compare the result with a realistic alternative
paragraphs: Ask for the packed measurements used in the quote. Compare that parcel with a feasible alternative using the same destination and eligible shipping method. Note the total cost of packaging services as well as any freight change. A smaller measured volume may produce no price change if the same billing increment applies. Make the choice using the quote and the protection required by the contents.

sections.heading: Examine the item that establishes each outer dimension
paragraphs: Picture a parcel containing folded shirts, a rigid stationery box and a framed print. The print may set the minimum length and width regardless of how tightly the shirts are compressed. The stationery box may determine the minimum height. A stack of shirts can fill the remaining space or push the height above that minimum. Ask which item sets the limiting dimension before paying for a service intended to reduce it. A smaller pile of shirts is only a cheaper parcel if the outer packing or billed weight actually changes.

In a soft-clothing-only parcel, the opportunity is different. Several thick sweaters may compress enough for a smaller carton. But a structured collar, delicate embellishment or material that should hold a particular shape deserves separate treatment. Inspect the product description and care information where available and decide which items you are comfortable compressing. Tell the warehouse about exceptions individually rather than assuming every item under the clothing category can be treated alike.

sections.heading: Compare protection for three distinct failures
paragraphs: First consider crushing. A rigid retail box or fragile shape can be damaged by surrounding weight even when its surface is covered. Second consider abrasion: two surfaces moving against one another may scratch in transit. Third consider free movement inside the outer carton. A well-wrapped object can still strike the carton if there is excessive unused space. Write down which failure you are trying to reduce so the proposed solution addresses the actual problem.

CSSBuy's forwarding material mentions bubble wrapping for fragile items and reinforced packing. Ask what the available service would do for your specific item. A request to protect a print's corners is different from asking to wrap a ceramic handle or keep metal parts separate from a polished surface. Stronger outer packaging can help in some situations while leaving a loose object free to move inside. Clarify what will be protected and how before evaluating the extra cost.

sections.heading: Calculate volume change without promising a rate change
paragraphs: Suppose a hypothetical outer carton is 45 by 35 by 30 centimetres. Its volume is 47,250 cubic centimetres. If compressing agreed soft items allows the height to fall to 24 centimetres with length and width unchanged, the new volume is 37,800 cubic centimetres. The volume falls by 9,450 cubic centimetres, or 20 percent. That arithmetic describes a box. It does not prove a 20-percent freight reduction because a route can price on a different weight, round within a billing bracket or apply other limits.

Now imagine that the rigid stationery box still requires a 30-centimetre outer height. Compressing the shirts may create empty space without reducing the outer volume at all. Asking the warehouse for the likely packed dimensions protects you from paying for an impressive-looking compression result that does little for freight. Check the current line's price treatment with the measured weight and dimensions. Do not import a divisor from a different route or a different platform.

sections.heading: Write a mixed-parcel instruction the packer can follow
paragraphs: Begin with the item reference and an unambiguous action. “Order A, two cotton shirts, may be compressed together. Order B, presentation box, retain its original carton and protect the corners. Order C, framed print, please advise on rigid outer protection before packing.” This example describes priorities without assuming the service offers a particular material or can guarantee a result. Ask the warehouse to flag conflicting requirements.

If retail packaging matters, define whether the box itself counts as merchandise. For a gift, creased packaging might make a sound product unsuitable. For a tool purchased for personal use, the printed sleeve may add little value while a moulded insert still protects important parts. Approve removal and retention separately for those components. If the packer cannot satisfy all requests within a single carton, compare separate shipping or a different grouping using the actual quotes available.

sections.heading: Reassess insurance and returns separately from packing
paragraphs: Protection against impact, the carrier's eligibility rules and any insurance terms are separate questions. Reinforcement cannot guarantee against all damage or make a restricted product acceptable to a route. If a particular object is valuable or unusually fragile, check the terms that apply to its contents, chosen shipping method and any available shipping protection. A generic description of reinforcement does not settle those points.

Also consider whether you may need to contact the seller about an unresolved warehouse concern. Removing retail packaging or compressing goods before you decide whether to keep them could complicate that conversation. Resolve a wrong variation or suspected missing accessory before authorizing unnecessary irreversible packing changes. For a parcel of several items, it may be reasonable to approve packing for the accepted goods while leaving one disputed unit out of the shipment.

sections.heading: Check the completed parcel against the request
paragraphs: When the warehouse supplies packed details, compare its reported dimensions and weight with the configuration you approved. If the height is unchanged, ask whether a rigid item sets the minimum rather than assuming the vacuum service was missed. If a protected item required more space, check whether the new carton remains within the chosen line's limits and whether the quote changes. Concentrate on the final cost of the complete acceptable configuration.

Keep the packing instruction, any reply and the approved quote with the parcel reference. At delivery, observe which packaging choices worked: whether a gift box remained presentable, whether wrapped items stayed separate and how much the soft goods expanded after unpacking. Use those observations as starting assumptions for a similar future order, then verify the new products' shapes and materials. The best packing decision is specific enough to protect what you care about and measurable enough to compare against a usable alternative.

sections.heading: Record which packaging instruction changed the outcome
paragraphs: If a second quote differs, isolate one change at a time where feasible. For example, first compare the same combined goods with and without the disposable shoe box, then consider adding protection to the retained product. Changing the line, outer carton and packaging services simultaneously leaves you unable to tell which choice drove the new cost or which part of the improvement could be repeated.

articles.title: Reconciling a CSSBuy shipping deposit with the final freight charge
articles.description: Compare the original estimate, the parcel measurements and any account adjustment after dispatch.

sections.heading: Keep the first estimate reproducible
paragraphs: Write down the destination, route, estimated weight and date used. Add any package dimensions you entered and indicate whether they came from the seller, your own estimate or the warehouse. A screenshot showing only a price leaves the most important inputs unknown. If the quote changes later, you want to know whether a different route, a different parcel or a revised measurement explains it.

sections.heading: Understand what CSSBuy charges at submission
paragraphs: The Buy For Me guide describes a shipping deposit based on an estimate, the chosen method and destination. It explains that the carrier verifies the final size and weight. Payment for the items and Chinese domestic delivery occurs earlier. When reconciling a payment statement, compare freight with freight. A wallet top-up, a purchase payment and the final parcel charge are separate entries with different purposes.

sections.heading: Work backwards from the packed box
paragraphs: Imagine two storage bins containing items that each weigh one kilogram. They may require different padding and outer boxes. If the final freight exceeds your model, look for packed measurements and the weight basis selected by that route. If the final figure is lower, CSSBuy says the relevant difference can be returned to the CSSBuy account after shipment. Check the account ledger as well as the card statement.

sections.heading: Ask support about one discrepancy at a time
paragraphs: Send the parcel number, original deposit, recorded final freight and the precise amount you cannot reconcile. If you expected a credit, include the dispatch date and identify the account entries you have already checked. If the problem is a measurement, request confirmation of the packed dimensions and units. These two requests involve different records and can be answered more readily when separated.

sections.heading: A worked ledger from purchase to freight credit
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative order, with invented amounts solely to show the arithmetic. You pay 210 yuan for the goods and 12 yuan to deliver them to the warehouse. Later you authorize an international shipping deposit of 160 yuan. After the carrier measurement is settled, suppose CSSBuy records final freight of 148 yuan and credits the 12-yuan difference to your account. The goods and domestic delivery total 222 yuan. With final freight included, the three components add to 370 yuan. The temporary sum of payments before the credit was 382 yuan.

A common reconciliation error is to add both 160 and 148 to the order total. The deposit and the settled freight refer to the same leg. Another error is to count a wallet top-up as an additional shipping cost. A top-up explains how a balance was funded. The later debit explains what it bought. If you funded the wallet in another currency, keep the conversion rate and provider charge in separate fields so that a currency movement does not appear to be a warehouse measurement issue.

If there are extra services, add them to the example only when you can identify a distinct charge. Packing material, insurance or a service recorded alongside freight may already be included in the displayed total. Check the itemization instead of making assumptions in either direction. A ledger that reconciles to the account should allow you to point to every component exactly once.

sections.heading: Trace the measurement that changed
paragraphs: Suppose your first estimate used a seller-provided item weight. The carrier checks the parcel as it travels, including the outer box and protective packing. Start by comparing the two objects that were weighed. An increase from an unpacked object to a complete parcel does not by itself indicate a weighing error. When the original figure came from an unrelated buyer's order, the comparison is even weaker because that buyer may have used different packaging or ordered a different quantity.

Next compare dimensions in the same units. A retail box placed inside an outer carton occupies more space than the retail box by itself. If the selected line takes dimensions into account, the height after packing may change the quote even when the weight difference on the scale is small. Consult the selected route's terms for its calculation. CSSBuy's general deposit explanation does not supply a universal divisor or billing increment applicable to every line.

Finally establish the point in time for both figures. A pre-packing estimate, a warehouse measurement and a carrier-verified final figure can be recorded on different dates. If support provides a revised measurement, write down which stage it represents. Otherwise it is easy to spend time comparing two estimates while overlooking the final amount that actually appears in the ledger.

sections.heading: Allocate freight to several purchases without overstating precision
paragraphs: If you are tracking the cost of each purchase, choose a method for allocating one final parcel charge across its contents. Dividing by item count is simple for several similar shirts. Dividing by individual weight may be more useful for a mix of books and small accessories. A bulky but light item can also make an equal-weight allocation misleading. There is no single accounting split implied by a combined carrier charge; state the method you chose.

For illustration, suppose the settled freight is 150 yuan and three similarly packaged orders weigh one, two and three kilograms. A purely weight-based split gives 25, 50 and 75 yuan. The three allocations add back to 150. If an additional rigid box was used only for the lightest product, you could record its separately itemized packing cost against that product. That is a budgeting decision. It does not change what CSSBuy charged for the parcel or establish what any individual item would have cost to ship on its own.

sections.heading: Send a question that identifies the unresolved line
paragraphs: A concise example might read, “For parcel P, I can see a deposit of 160 yuan and a final shipping record of 148 yuan. Could you identify the ledger entry for the 12-yuan adjustment?” Replace the illustrative figures with the actual amounts. Give the dispatch date and the currency, and explain whether the question concerns a CSSBuy wallet transaction or an external payment statement. Keep payment-card numbers and unrelated account details out of screenshots.

A measurement enquiry needs a different question. For example, ask for the carrier-verified packed dimensions, measured weight and applicable route when the final freight differs from the model you saved. Include the input values from your own estimate so support can see what you compared. If the final amount includes services, ask which entries represent freight and which represent those services. Do not ask a carrier to locate a wallet credit or expect the payment provider to know a parcel's packed dimensions.

sections.heading: Close the record when all entries reconcile
paragraphs: Keep the original estimate, deposit receipt, final freight record and any later credit together with the parcel number. If the parcel covered multiple orders, include the item references as well. When you review the cost later, compare it with another parcel only after matching route, destination, packing and time period. Two similarly heavy shipments can still be poor comparisons if one included bulky boxes or additional protection.

The most useful lesson from a previous charge is usually a better input for the next estimate. You might learn that a particular boxed item needs a larger outer carton, or that a seller's published weight excludes packaging. Record that observation beside the dimensions you actually received. You can then make a more realistic preliminary budget while continuing to use the current route quote and the new parcel's own final measurements.

If the account shows a separate refund unrelated to the parcel, leave it on its original transaction. Matching two entries only because the numbers are equal can hide an unsettled difference. Use the parcel reference, transaction description and posting date together to confirm the link.

articles.title: Using CSSBuy My Parcel to trace a shipment and report a delivery issue
articles.description: Follow the correct parcel number from dispatch to receipt and attach a clear after-sales note if goods arrive damaged or incomplete.

sections.heading: Switch from the item record to the parcel record
paragraphs: A seller can deliver goods to the warehouse long before the overseas parcel is sent. CSSBuy's Buy For Me guide directs users to My Parcel in the User Center after dispatch. Before asking a carrier to trace an order, establish whether you have a seller tracking number or the international parcel number. Keep both if a missing item could have disappeared on either leg.

sections.heading: Write down the last verifiable event
paragraphs: Copy the carrier name, tracking number, date, time zone if available and the actual status text. A shipping label, an acceptance scan and a delivery scan establish different things. If the carrier has no visible event yet, report that observation without treating it as proof of loss. In a support note, ask which handoff was completed and whether a different last-mile number is available for your parcel.

sections.heading: Reconstruct what was packed
paragraphs: Use the list of orders submitted in the parcel and compare it with the items you actually received. Photograph the outer box, label, packaging condition and contents before discarding anything. If an accessory seems absent, check inserts and smaller internal packets. State which order and selected variant you expected, including the quantity. Avoid publishing a delivery label with your full address or phone number.

sections.heading: Contact the service tied to the problem
paragraphs: CSSBuy describes after-sales notes on the relevant My Parcel entry. For a shipment issue, include the parcel reference and evidence of its condition. For a defect in a particular item, add its seller order and any warranty paperwork. Ask what further documentation and response deadline apply to the case. Keep the parcel investigation and the seller's response in the same file so that later updates can be matched accurately.

sections.heading: Identify which parcel could contain the missing item
paragraphs: Before tracing anything, pull up the list of warehouse orders you actually submitted. Suppose two similar pencil cases came from the same seller and only one was selected for overseas shipping. If the other case is still in storage, an apparently incomplete home delivery may match the parcel exactly. Conversely, if both appear on the same waybill and only one is present, you have a specific shortage to investigate. Record the item references and selected quantities rather than relying on thumbnails.

If you submitted two international parcels together, check their waybills separately. They may move through different carrier facilities or reach the destination on different days. Do not treat the arrival of the first as proof that all goods should already be at your door. Put the missing order next to the waybill that actually lists it. This one step can distinguish a second parcel still travelling from a genuine issue in a parcel already delivered.

sections.heading: Build a timeline that separates the seller and carrier
paragraphs: Take the last few confirmed events and arrange them by date: seller dispatch to the warehouse, warehouse receipt, parcel submission, international dispatch and the carrier's latest scan. The event names are more useful than copying every line of an app notification. A seller's domestic delivery means the package reached the domestic address associated with the purchase. It does not show that the international carrier received your consolidated box.

For a parcel with no apparent movement, note which number you entered and which carrier displayed the status. Some references identify orders rather than transport consignments. A shipping label can exist before the first visible carrier acceptance. If an account page indicates dispatch but the public tracker has no matching event, ask CSSBuy for confirmation of the handoff and the correct tracking number. Where appropriate, ask whether a separate local number exists for delivery in your country.

sections.heading: Handle an exception according to what it actually says
paragraphs: If tracking reports a failed delivery attempt, check the carrier's official instructions, the address used and any recipient contact details that might need attention. A recipient absent at delivery, a missing apartment number and a parcel held for collection each call for different actions. Contact the party named by the carrier and keep CSSBuy's parcel record updated. Avoid posting your full delivery label or private contact information in a public tracking discussion.

If tracking says delivered but the parcel is absent, first check the delivery details, any designated receiving area and whether someone authorized to receive it accepted it. Ask the carrier what proof of delivery is available. Note which checks you completed and when. If no parcel is found, give CSSBuy the timeline, the international reference and the carrier's reply. Make clear that the issue is a delivery record you cannot reconcile, rather than stating that the merchant failed to ship.

sections.heading: Document a delivered parcel before rearranging its contents
paragraphs: When a box is torn, crushed or unusually light, keep the original packing and record its condition promptly. Take a whole-box view that ties the evidence to the waybill, then close views of damage or broken tape. Photograph the internal arrangement as you remove goods. A close view of a broken part is helpful, but without the rest of the packaging it may be difficult to establish which item and shipment it came from.

Compare what you find with the parcel inventory. Small accessories can sit inside sleeves, retail inserts or a pocket in the main product. Check these places before reporting a shortage. If the warehouse images show the accessory before packing, preserve them alongside the delivery photos and the order confirmation. If there is no photo showing it, say so. A good report distinguishes the item that clearly arrived damaged from a component whose earlier presence remains uncertain.

sections.heading: Choose the right after-sales question
paragraphs: A dent to the outer shipping carton with undamaged goods may matter little for a utilitarian purchase. The same dent can be material when a collectible retail box was part of what you bought. Explain the specific loss in relation to your order and packing request. If the issue is a product function that first fails after use, retain the purchase receipt and warranty documentation and consult the seller-related after-sales process. A carrier investigation into external damage is unlikely to resolve a technical fault without other evidence.

For a parcel issue, CSSBuy directs buyers to add an after-sales note on the relevant My Parcel entry. Include the waybill, affected item reference, actual event time and the action you are asking for. A focused message might request a trace, the warehouse packing record, the applicable carrier claim procedure or instructions for contacting the seller. Ask about any evidence deadline promptly. Keep the original images and retain the packaging until you know what the investigating party requires.

sections.heading: Reconcile the final answer with the original problem
paragraphs: An internal trace can establish a handoff without establishing successful delivery. A seller can authorize an exchange without the replacement yet reaching the warehouse. A carrier can acknowledge a complaint without accepting liability or determining compensation. Record the outcome at the correct level and keep any remaining action open. If the agent asks for an additional photo, send the requested angle and explain what it shows instead of resending the entire original message.

At completion, save the resolution next to the parcel number and affected order. If a missing item was found in a second waybill, record that second reference. If the merchant agreed to replace a component, track that new shipment separately. If a carrier or seller declined a claim, keep the stated reason with the applicable terms. This record gives you a reliable account of what happened to your goods and a practical basis for improving packing, tracking or evidence collection on your next shipment.

sections.heading: Save the correct contact reference
paragraphs: When a carrier opens its own investigation, record that case number separately from the tracking number and your CSSBuy parcel reference. A follow-up to the carrier can then reach the existing enquiry, while the CSSBuy order note continues to show which warehouse items and waybill the case concerns.

faq.q: Where do I start with a Weidian find?
faq.a: Open its source listing, confirm the seller and selected variant, then paste the item link into CSSBuy's search field and review the order preview.

faq.q: What if CSSBuy cannot load the product link?
faq.a: The Buy For Me guide points to Expert Buy. Supply the direct listing, option text, price and quantity so the intended purchase can be identified.

faq.q: Can CSSBuy search for an item by name?
faq.a: Its official ordering guide lists product-name search across Taobao, Tmall and 1688. Check the seller and specification of any match before ordering.

faq.q: Can a 1688 listing require multiple units?
faq.a: Yes. CSSBuy directs buyers to the supplier's minimum. Confirm whether it applies to an individual colour, pack or the whole order.

faq.q: What does the first CSSBuy payment cover?
faq.a: The Buy For Me guide describes payment for the item and Chinese domestic delivery at this stage. International freight comes when the warehouse parcel is submitted.

faq.q: How do I prevent a colour substitution?
faq.a: Record the seller's exact option text and use the order note to request contact before the buyer accepts a substitute.

faq.q: When are CSSBuy warehouse photos taken?
faq.a: The purchasing guide places inspection and photography after warehouse arrival. Open the relevant stored item to review available images.

faq.q: Are all 1688 goods inspected under the same standard as other orders?
faq.a: CSSBuy flags a separate inspection standard for 1688. Check what can be inspected on your particular order before relying on a specific check.

faq.q: How should I request a garment measurement?
faq.a: Identify the item and specify the unit, both endpoints and whether the garment should lie flat. Compare the result with a garment measured in the same way.

faq.q: When does free warehouse storage begin?
faq.a: CSSBuy's FAQ starts the 90-day period when the order reaches In Warehouse status. Check the date for each order individually.

faq.q: What is the published storage extension price?
faq.a: CSSBuy's public FAQ lists 15 yuan per order per month after the standard free period. Verify the current charge and new expiry date in your account.

faq.q: Can unpaid, expired storage lead to disposal?
faq.a: Yes. CSSBuy warns that unshipped items without an extension can be treated as abandoned and destroyed after the free period.

faq.q: Can CSSBuy return a stored item to its seller?
faq.a: The official FAQ requires seller acceptance, less than seven days in the warehouse and payment of return postage. Contact CSSBuy promptly with the order number.

faq.q: What is Ship For Me used for?
faq.a: You buy from the merchant yourself and send the purchase to CSSBuy for forwarding. Buy For Me is the purchasing-agent workflow.

faq.q: Where can I find my CSSBuy forwarding address?
faq.a: Get it from your member center and preserve every receiving field shown when you enter it with the merchant.

faq.q: Can separate packages be consolidated?
faq.a: CSSBuy offers warehouse consolidation. Check that all expected items have arrived and are eligible for the chosen international route.

faq.q: When is vacuum packing worth considering?
faq.a: Consider it for compressible clothing where reducing the packed volume could affect freight. Check whether other rigid items still set the box dimensions.

faq.q: Can I request extra protection for fragile items?
faq.a: CSSBuy describes reinforced packaging and bubble wrapping. Identify the item and fragile surfaces and ask what protection is available.

faq.q: Why can the final international fee differ from the deposit?
faq.a: CSSBuy estimates the deposit and calculates final freight using carrier-verified parcel size and weight. Compare the same parcel and route when reviewing the adjustment.

faq.q: Where do I track the international parcel?
faq.a: Open My Parcel in the User Center after dispatch. Use the parcel tracking number rather than the seller's domestic number.

faq.q: How do I report a problem after delivery?
faq.a: Open the relevant My Parcel entry and add an after-sales note with the order number, parcel number and evidence of the issue.
